prompt: Why are many organizations dropping traditional performance appraisals (Cappelli & Tavis, 2016)?
modelAnswer: Three core arguments: (1) the return of people development – firms must grow talent and need frequent coaching rather than a yearly backward-looking rating; (2) the need for agility – annual goals become obsolete quickly, so firms use short-term goals and frequent check-ins; (3) the centrality of teamwork – individual ratings and rankings undermine collaboration, while work is done in teams. In addition, forced distribution has well-known disadvantages: demotivation of the middle, infighting, admin cost, horse-trading, no value for diversity, short-termism. Firms still need decisions on pay and promotion, so they replace rather than abolish evaluation.

prompt: What must a performance theory specify before an organization can measure performance (Latham, Sulsky & Macdonald, 2007)?
modelAnswer: (a) The relevant performance dimensions; (b) the performance standards or expectations associated with each performance level; (c) how situational constraints should be weighted, if at all; (d) the number of performance levels or gradients; (e) whether performance is judged against absolute standards or by relative comparison with others. Without these, manager and employee can disagree about what “good performance” means, as in the role play.

prompt: Analyse Pixelwerk's performance management system. What behaviours does it encourage and why does it fail?
modelAnswer: The system measures quantitative output (code, tickets, deadlines) for both groups, once a year, with a forced ranking. Behaviour: R&D avoids risk because failures lower ratings – exactly the opposite of the innovation it needs (key problem: lack of innovation, like Beach House); live-ops stops cooperating because colleagues are rivals on the curve (infighting, reduced collaboration). Forced distribution also demotivates the middle and invites horse-trading. In Latham et al.'s terms, performance dimensions are not defined per job, and relative standards replace absolute ones. The system serves accountability only, not development or communication.

prompt: Design a new performance management system for Pixelwerk.
modelAnswer: Purpose: development and communication first, accountability for pay decisions separately. Segment the system, because the A-Team-style R&D cannot be managed like the “Tweakers”: R&D – autonomy, qualitative indicators (quality of experiments, learning, ideas tested), team goals, frequent peer and lead feedback, protection for failed experiments; live-ops – clearer quantitative indicators (stability, response times, player satisfaction) combined with team goals to restore cooperation. Replace the forced curve with absolute standards and continuous check-ins (Cappelli & Tavis); decouple developmental conversations from the annual pay decision. Analyse externalities: count of experiments could be gamed; tickets closed can reduce quality – so combine indicators and judgement.
keyPoints: Segments R&D vs live-ops with justification
